recentItems.title: Looney Tunes | Wile E. Coyote vs Road Runner Episodes Compilation | Vol. 14 | Warner Classics
recentItems.description:
Watch Wile. E. Coyote chase the Road Runner with all his tools and tricks, full Looney Tunes episodes from the 40's, 50's and 60's!

Episodes Included:
Going! Going! Gosh! (1952): The Coyote makes various attempts to get the Road Runner such as with an explosive-tipped arrow, by shooting himself out of a sling shot and by covering the road with quick drying cement.

Fast and Furry-ous (1949): Wile E. Coyote makes 11 disastrous attempts to catch the Roadrunner.

Zipping Along (1953): The Road Runner outpaces a speeding locomotive and then repeatedly runs over and knocks down the Coyote at an intersection.

Stop! Look! and Hasten! (1954): The Coyote employs a series of devices to try to capture the Road Runner.

Rushing Roulette (1965): The Coyote tries all sorts of methods to catch the Roadrunner.

Boulder Wham (1965): Wile E. Coyote finds himself stuck on the other side of a cliff with the road runner on the other side. He makes many unsucessful attempts to cross the cliff gap.

Chaser on the Rocks (1965): Crazy from the heat, Wile E. Coyote sets up a trap for the Road Runner with a glass of lemonade

recentItems.description:
Enjoy classic Full Tom and Jerry episodes with some of our favorite hilarious moments from 40's, 50's and 60's!

Episodes in order:
The Midnight Snack (1941): Jerry decides to have a midnight snack of cheese but Tom presents a problem with that idea.

Little Runaway (1952): Tom plans on capturing an escaped baby seal from the circus for the big reward but Jerry befriends the seal and tries to stop him.

Mouse Trouble (1944): Tom starts to read a book called "How to Catch a Mouse." Although the traps are set for Jerry... the clever mouse thwarts Tom's plan to catch him, and Tom goes through all the traps in a brutal way.

Tee for Two (1945): Tom uses Jerry as a tee at the golf course but soon after things start to go poorly for the cat.

Smitten Kitten (1952): Jerry has flashbacks when he sees Tom interested in a female cat.

Landing Stripling (1962): Jerry and a helmet-wearing bird give Tom a difficult time.

recentItems.title: Looney Tunes | Yosemite Sam, Bugs Bunny Mega Compilation | Warner Classics
recentItems.description:
Yosemite Sam is after Bugs Bunny again as a knight, hunter, pirate, and more in these classic hilarious Looney Tunes episode moments!

Episodes in order:
Knighty Knight Bugs (1958): Bugs is a hapless court jester who sneaks into the villain's castle while Black Knight Sam is snoozing. Bugs makes off with the sword with Sam chasing him the whole way and holes up in Sam's castle not letting him in. As Bugs tries to sneak out Sam and his fire breathing lizard sneak in and all three of them find themselves in the explosives room. When the lizard sneezes he converts the entire turret of the castle into a rocket heading straight for the moon.

Mutiny on the Bunny (1950): Shanghai Sam tricks Bugs into sailing with him and then makes him do all the work. Bugs takes control of the boat angering Sam who shoots at the boat. When the boat sinks Sam and Bugs have to use the lifeboat to get back to shore.

Piker's Peak (1957): Bugs and Sam are in a race to see who can climb to the top of Schmatterhorn first and win 50,000 cronkites. Sam tries every trick he knows to make Bugs lose the race, but all these tricks backfire on him and he loses the race.

Rabbitson Crusoe (1956): Sam, playing Crusoe, lives on one of three little islands where he is trapped because of a shark named Dopey Dick. When Bugs appears on the island, Sam tries to eat him because he is tired of eating coconuts everyday, but through a series of pranks Bugs manages to get away.

Captain Hareblower (1954): Captain Bugs of his ship battles Pirate Yosemite Sam.

Bunker Hill Bunny (1950): The historic Revolutionary War battle at Bagel Heights is fought between Bugs and Yosemite.

Hare Trimmed (1953): Granny finds herself in a love triangle between Sam and Bugs both fighting for her hand in marriage, Sam for money, Bugs for good deeds. Sam tries to seduce her and Bugs challenges Sam to a gentlemen's dual. Bugs cleverly disguises himself as Granny and tricks Sam into doing a lot of painful things.

It's Election Day in America as Bill McKay (Robert Redford), the son of the former Governor and underdog candidate, wins the presidency.

Subscribe to Warner Classics: https://www.youtube.com/channel/UCU0rIMU3k_AsVA8d6N1B03w?sub_confirmation=1

About The Candidate (Theatrical Release - June 30, 1972):
More powerful today than at the time of its 1972 release, The Candidate is a timeless tale of contemporary politics; expertly written by Oscar winner Jeremy Larner.

Robert Redford plays Bill McKay, an idealistic California attorney running for office in this marvelous, biting, satire on media-age political campaigns.

The stellar cast includes Peter Boyle and Melvyn Douglas, who also give memorable performances.

Starring: Robert Redford, Peter Boyle, Melvyn Douglas
Directed by: Michael Ritchie

About Casablanca (Theatrical Release - November 26, 1942):
Academy Award winners Humphrey Bogart and Ingrid Bergman light up the screen in one of the most enduring romances in movie history--Casablanca. Rick Blaine (Bogart--The African Queen, The Caine Mutiny) owns a nightclub in Vichy-controlled Casablanca, frequented by refugees desperate to escape German domination. Despite the ever-present human misery, Rick manages to remain uninvolved in World War II now raging across Europe and Northern Africa. But all that changes when Ilsa Lund (Bergman--Gaslight, Notorious) walks through the front door of Rick's club--Rick must now choose between a life with the woman he loves and becoming the hero that both she and the world need.​

Starring:  Humphrey Bogart as Rick, Ingrid Bergman as Ilsa
Directed by: Michael Curtiz

Welcome to Warner Classics - your gateway to the enchanting world of timeless movies and iconic performances from the Golden Age of Hollywood! Dive into a treasure trove of cinematic splendor, where every clip tells a story and every scene captivates the soul.

Join us on a journey through the annals of film history as we showcase unforgettable moments from the silver screen. Including Hollywood's brightest stars, our channel is a celebration of artistry and nostalgia that will transport you to a bygone era of glamour and sophistication.

recentItems.title: Tom and Jerry | Halloween Mega Compilation | Warner Classics
recentItems.description:
Jump into Spooky Season with full episodes of Tom and Jerry Halloween themed featuring Witches, Ghosts, and magical potions! 

Episodes in order:
The Invisible Mouse (1947): Jerry turns invisible after diving into a bottle of invisible ink and then gets back at Tom.

Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Mouse (1947): Jerry drinks a potion that makes him grow to the size of a giant. He decides to go after Tom, because THIS time he's bigger. Once the potion wears off, Tom drinks some of it, and he gets bigger. They do this over and over again. Academy Award nominee for 1948 Best Short Subject.

Fraidy Cat (1942): After Tom gets scared from listening to The Witching Hour on the radio Jerry schemes a way to keep him scared.

The Flying Sorceress (1956): Tom steals a witch's flying broom so he can scare the wits out of Jerry.
 
The Missing Mouse (1953): Jerry takes advantage of Tom's fear of an exploding white mouse by dunking himself in white shoe polish.

Purr-Chance to Dream (1967): Tom isn't sleeping well and keeps having nightmares about getting beat up by a bulldog.

Is There A Doctor In The Mouse (1964): Drinking a potion he mixed together helps Jerry beat Tom to all the food.

recentItems.title: Looney Tunes | Halloween Episodes Compilation | Warner Classics
recentItems.description:
Celebrate Halloween with these iconic Looney Tunes moments featuring Bugs Bunny, Witch Hazel, Porky Pig, Sylvester and Daffy Duck.

Episodes in order:
Transylvania 6-5000 (1963): While tunneling to Pittsburgh, Bugs Bunny mistakenly surfaces in Transylvania. He asks for directions at a mysterious castle, where he meets a vampire named Count Bloodcount. Now, with the count chasing him, Bugs finds a book with magic words that he uses against Bloodcount.

Hair-Raising Hare (1946): A mad scientist sends a sexy rabbit-robot to lure Bugs in as food for his monster. Bugs gets lured in by the robot and when he's face to face with the monster he freezes in a 'yipes!' position and then the long chase begins.

Broom-Stick Bunny (1956): Bugs makes a visit to Witch Hazel who is infatuated with her own ugliness and needs a rabit for her stew...

Claws for Alarm (1954): Porky and his pet, Sylvester, stay the night in a big, scary mansion.

Hyde and Hare (1955): Bugs gets himself adopted as a pet by a kindly soul who has been feeding him carrots every day. Bugs' friend turns out to be Dr. Jekyll who drinks his evil potion and turns into a monster. Bugs ended up drinking some of the potion and once back in the park he is transformed into a monstrous rabbit.

Bewitched Bunny (1954): Bugs enters the fairytale world to go save Hansel and Gretel from the witch.

A Witch's Tangled Hare (1959): In search of poetic inspiration, William Shakespeare comes across the castle of Macbeth and finds Witch Hazel chasing Bugs Bunny therein. The Bard jots down their dialogue as possibilities for dramatic situations.

recentItems.description:
After Luke's (Paul Newman) attempted prison escape he is reprimanded by The Captain (Strother Martin) about his "Failure to communicate."

Watch Now! https://www.warnerbros.com/movies/cool-hand-luke

About Cool Hand Luke (October 31, 1967):
Academy Award winner Paul Newman stars with George Kennedy in this story of a man who will not surrender to authority--even at the cost of his life. When Luke Jackson (Newman) is sentenced to a Southern prison for a minor infraction, his intelligence, calm under pressure and inability to accept defeat soon gain him the respect of his fellow inmates on the chain gang--and the nickname Cool Hand Luke. But they also earn Luke the enmity of the warden, who cannot allow any inmate to challenge his authority. When Luke's mother dies, he decides to escape ... and he will not allow anyone to stop him.

recentItems.title: Looney Tunes | Classic Tweety Bird & Sylvester Compilation | Vol. 9 | Warner Classics
recentItems.description:
Enjoy full episodes of iconic Tweety bird and Sylvester the cat from the Looney Tunes Classic Shorts series! 

Episodes in order:
Ain't She Tweet (1952): Tweety gets bought by Granny, and Sylvester tries all sorts of devices to defeat the dogs guarding Tweety in the house.

A Bird in a Guilty Cage (1952): Mannequins and clothes go flying in this Sylvester and Tweety chase in a department store.

The Last Hungry Cat (1961): In Hitchcock form this cartoon follows Sylvester after he thinks he has killed Tweety. When he returns to the house and finds Tweety alive he kisses him only to be hit by Granny for touching the bird.

Tweety's S.O.S. (1951): Sylvester finds Tweety aboard an ocean liner with Granny. Granny tries to protect Tweety but has one problem: She has terrible vision. Sylvester uses this to his advantage by keeping her glasses away from her to have a chance at Tweety. However, Tweety keeps returning Granny's glasses.

The Jet Cage (1962): Granny orders a new-fangled flying bird cage for Tweety, jet-powered and complete with crash helmet. Tweety tries it out in the backyard and heckles Sylvester. Sylvester tries hard to catch him but fails and ends up in bandages.

All Abir-r-rd! (1950): Tweety is put aboard a train bound for Gower Gulch and runs into the devious Sylvester.
